macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks rebound as investors await midterm results
items.summary: The S&P 500 and Nasdaq rose about 0.6% and 1.1%, respectively, while the Dow fell roughly 0.3% in afternoon trading. Investors were weighing earnings and uncertainty surrounding the U.S. midterm elections.[1]

items.title: RBA raises interest rate to 4.85%
items.summary: The Reserve Bank of Australia raised its cash rate by 25 basis points to 4.85% in a 6–3 vote, the highest level since 2008. The decision reflected upwardly revised inflation forecasts, with inflation expected to remain above target for longer.[2][5]

items.title: Apple shares fall after margin outlook disappoints
items.summary: Apple shares declined after the company reported better-than-expected quarterly results but forecast weaker holiday-quarter gross margins because of rising memory-chip costs. Services revenue growth guidance also fell short of Wall Street expectations.[1][5]

items.title: Asian and European stocks pressured by technology selloff
items.summary: Asian equities outside Japan fell 1.4%, led by declines of as much as 4.1% in South Korea and 3.6% in Taiwan. European markets also traded lower as Apple’s outlook weighed on technology shares.[5][7]

items.title: PBOC increases foreign-exchange reserve requirement
items.summary: China’s central bank said it would raise the foreign-exchange reserve requirement ratio for financial institutions by two percentage points to 6%.[2]

items.title: Oil rebounds amid geopolitical uncertainty
items.summary: Brent crude recovered modestly after Monday’s decline as markets assessed Middle East developments and the outlook for peace talks. Brent traded near $105 per barrel in Asian trading.[5]

items.title: AMD and other major companies due to report earnings
items.summary: Investors were focused on after-hours earnings from AMD and Super Micro Computer, alongside reports from companies including Pfizer, Shopify and Booking Holdings. AMD expectations centered on strong data-center growth.[5][9][10]

items.title: Pfizer raises full-year revenue guidance
items.summary: Pfizer reported third-quarter revenue above expectations and increased its full-year revenue outlook.[10]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin and major cryptocurrencies fall
items.summary: The global crypto market capitalization declined 0.7% to $2.678 trillion over 24 hours. Bitcoin fell 2.2% to about $76,829, while Ethereum, BNB, XRP and Solana also posted losses; liquidations reached approximately $176 million.[5]

items.title: New Jersey drops Coinbase staking case
items.summary: New Jersey reportedly withdrew its staking lawsuit against Coinbase and lifted its cease-and-desist order, allowing users in the state to resume staking.[1][4]

items.title: NEAR governance approves lower token issuance
items.summary: NEAR’s House of Stake approved a plan to reduce the network’s maximum annual issuance rate from 2.5% to 1.6%, phased in over 24 months.[2][4]

items.title: Consensys launches institutional cross-ledger infrastructure
items.summary: Consensys introduced a technology stack designed to let banks route and settle transactions across independent ledgers without transferring the underlying assets.[2]

items.title: Mercado Bitcoin reports security incident
items.summary: Brazilian exchange Mercado Bitcoin temporarily suspended service access after detecting a security incident involving approximately $38 million in assets. About $11 million had reportedly been frozen, while the exchange said customers would not lose assets.[6]

items.title: CFTC crypto rule proposal advances
items.summary: The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission sent a proposed cryptocurrency rule to the White House for review, continuing efforts to establish a digital-asset regulatory framework after broader legislation stalled in the Senate.[7]

items.title: Strategy adds 810 Bitcoin
items.summary: Strategy reportedly purchased another 810 BTC, bringing its stated holdings to 849,327 Bitcoin.[5]

items.title: Liquid Network restores one-to-one Bitcoin backing
items.summary: Liquid Federation said the network’s Bitcoin reserves were fully restored, re-establishing one-to-one backing for LBTC and enabling transfers between Bitcoin and Liquid through participating swap providers.[6]

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Anthropic introduces Claude Opus 5.5
items.summary: Anthropic announced Claude Opus 5.5, describing it as a leading model for agentic coding and knowledge work. The company says it costs 40% less to run than Claude Opus 5 on typical workloads.

items.title: Snowflake expands its agentic AI platform
items.summary: Snowflake announced a Business Ontology framework, expanded agent governance through Cortex AI Gateway, autonomous data-engineering capabilities, and a preview of Cortex Training for adapting open-weight models to proprietary information.

items.title: Mistral releases Large 4 for cybersecurity applications
items.summary: Mistral AI publicly released Large 4, an upgraded model shaped by testing with government and corporate users. The release emphasizes cybersecurity and gives organizations more control through open model weights.

items.title: AI infrastructure spending pushes corporate debt higher
items.summary: A report cited by The Economic Times says AI infrastructure investment has helped drive debt among the so-called Magnificent Seven companies up 45% to $578 billion. The trend highlights the increasing capital intensity of frontier AI deployment.

items.title: South Korea plans to double AI and semiconductor spending
items.summary: South Korea announced plans to double spending on artificial intelligence and semiconductors in 2027 to a record level. The government also linked the investment to modernizing national defense capabilities.

items.title: Deep Principle unveils Hydrogen-1.0 science model
items.summary: Deep Principle released Hydrogen-1.0, an open-weight model aimed at scientific research and materials discovery. The company reported a 38.3% score on its FSR evaluation, while demonstrations have not yet established real-world synthesis or laboratory operation.

items.title: Prefrontal reports major gains from Latent Sparse Attention
items.summary: Prefrontal published research on Latent Sparse Attention, reporting substantially faster attention processing for very long contexts, including up to 72.4 times faster processing at 10 million tokens. The reported results include faster prefill and time to first token.

items.title: Trajectory raises $45 million for continuous-feedback AI training
items.summary: AI startup Trajectory raised a Sequoia-led $45 million Series A at a reported $300 million valuation. Its platform is designed to help companies train models through continuous feedback without requiring dedicated AI research teams.

items.title: GitHub announces Copilot Code Review Max
items.summary: GitHub unveiled Copilot Code Review Max, which uses multiple AI review agents in parallel and an aggregator to reconcile findings and recheck accuracy. The announcement was made at GitHub Universe 2026.

items.title: DeepSeek reportedly plans Huawei-based training infrastructure
items.summary: Industry sources cited by AIB say DeepSeek plans to train its V5 model primarily on Huawei Ascend 950 chips in 2027. The development would underscore China’s continued effort to build frontier AI around domestic semiconductor infrastructure.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Bethesda reveals The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel
items.summary: Bethesda unveiled the official subtitle and logo for its next major role-playing game, The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel, during its 40th-anniversary event. No release date, gameplay footage, or detailed mechanics were announced.[1]

items.title: Grand Theft Auto VI preload begins November 10
items.summary: Rockstar and PlayStation announced that digital preloading for Grand Theft Auto VI will begin November 10. The game may require up to 212 GB of storage, with platform-specific midnight release timing.[7][9]

items.title: Borderlands franchise surpasses 100 million sales
items.summary: Gearbox announced that the Borderlands franchise has sold more than 100 million copies worldwide. The studio is also continuing development of additional Borderlands 4 content.[1][3]

items.title: Phantom Blade Zero sells 4 million copies in 72 hours
items.summary: S-GAME reported that Phantom Blade Zero sold more than four million copies during its first 72 hours after launching digitally for PC and PlayStation 5 on October 29.[5]

items.title: Thief: The Dark Project Remastered dated for December 3
items.summary: Nightdive Studios set December 3, 2026, as the release date for Thief: The Dark Project Remastered. The remaster will launch across PC, PlayStation, Xbox, and Nintendo platforms and includes a new campaign, The Tarnished Mirror.[8]

items.title: PlayStation announces new seasonal updates and releases
items.summary: PlayStation highlighted the launch of Sonic Racing: CrossWorlds Year Two content, new Helldivers 2 Terminid types and bug caves, and the November 13 release of sci-fi horror game Derelikt on PS5.[7]

items.title: Nagoshi Studio reportedly shuts down after funding loss
items.summary: Nagoshi Studio, founded by Yakuza creator Toshihiro Nagoshi, has reportedly closed after NetEase withdrew funding from its debut project, Gang of Dragon.[3]

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: Apple reports stronger revenue as iPhone sales rise
items.summary: Apple posted better-than-expected revenue in its latest quarter, driven by stronger iPhone sales as John Ternus assumes the chief executive role.[4]

items.title: Marvell agrees to acquire Lumentum in major stock deal
items.summary: Marvell Technology announced an agreement to acquire optical-components maker Lumentum in an all-stock transaction reportedly valued at roughly $102.6 billion to $115 billion.[4][6]

items.title: Supermarket freezers targeted in apparent cyberattacks
items.summary: Supermarket freezer systems in several European countries were reportedly disrupted in apparent cyberattacks, highlighting vulnerabilities in connected retail infrastructure.[5]

items.title: GMO apologizes after security breaches
items.summary: Japanese online-services company GMO apologized for security breaches and promised compensation, according to an Associated Press technology roundup.[5]

items.title: Meta delays new business terms after backlash
items.summary: Meta postponed changes to its business terms following criticism over provisions that could have enabled web scraping of news websites.[5]

items.title: Apple smart-home robot reportedly delayed
items.summary: Apple’s planned smart-home robot may not launch until 2028, with software development reportedly still underway despite hardware being ready.[6]

items.title: Snap reportedly settles social-media addiction lawsuit
items.summary: Snap is reportedly finalizing a settlement with two teenagers who alleged that excessive use of Snapchat harmed their mental health, avoiding a trial in Los Angeles.[6]

items.title: New York Times sues Brave over alleged content scraping
items.summary: The New York Times reportedly sued the Brave browser, alleging unauthorized scraping of its content and tools that could help users bypass paywalls.[6]

items.title: Google opens UK offices to trade-union recruitment
items.summary: Google is partnering with the Prospect union to allow recruitment access at its King’s Cross headquarters after changes to UK labor rules.[6]
